correct_completion: she presented the case with confidence.
full_sentence: Her arguments carefully prepared, she presented the case with confidence.
acceptable_variants: she argued the case with assurance.
she made the case with confidence.

options.why_wrong: This is another participle phrase with no finite verb, so it cannot serve as the main clause.

options.text: to present the case with confidence.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive phrase has no subject and no finite verb, so the sentence still lacks a main clause.

options.text: she presented the case with confidence.
because she had presented the case with confidence.
options.why_wrong: 'Because' turns the stem into a subordinate clause and refers to a finished action, which breaks the absolute structure.

grammar_focus: Verbless absolute clauses followed by a main clause
explanation: A verbless absolute clause has its own subject, here 'arguments', plus a participle, and it adds background to the main clause that follows. Turkish speakers may insert a finite verb into the absolute part or repeat the subject, because Turkish participial structures are often used more freely in such positions.
translation: Argümanları özenle hazırlanmış halde, davayı özgüvenle sundu.
